cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is guiding God's people through the wilderness after leaving Egypt. Now they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea. It's the long way around, friend.

cards.question: Why does Israel take the long way toward the Red Sea?

answers.text: To go around the land of Edom

cards.question: On the long road around Edom, the people grow impatient.

cards.text: You know when the GPS adds forty minutes and somebody in the back seat sighs real LOUD? Now picture a whole nation in that back seat, and they don't keep it to themselves.

cards.question: The impatient people speak against God and against ___.
The people ask why they were led out of Egypt to die in the wilderness. They say there is no ___ or ___.

cards.text: Then they say, "we detest this wretched food!" Friend, I bake cookies all day long, and even I have given a sugar cookie the side-eye on a long week.

cards.question: After the people speak against Him, what does the LORD send among them?
Only a few of the Israelites are bitten by the venomous snakes.

cards.text: Snakes in the camp, and people bitten and dying. Then the same people who spoke against Moses come walking right up to him.

cards.question: The people tell Moses they have ___ by speaking against the LORD and against him.
What do the people ask Moses to do for them?

answers.text: Intercede so the LORD takes the snakes away
Lead them back down to Egypt
Build a wall around the camp

cards.text: So Moses interceded for the people, the very ones who just spoke against him. That's a big heart, friend, and mine would've been right there too, just crying into my mustache the WHOLE prayer.

cards.question: After Moses intercedes, what does the LORD tell him to make?

answers.text: A fiery serpent on a pole

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses that anyone who is bitten and ___ at the serpent on the pole will live.
Moses makes the snake for the pole out of ___.
Only the first bitten person to look at the bronze snake would live.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It retells the impatience that card 3 already asked about and adds nothing new from the passage. The hint that they 'don't keep it to themselves' belongs to verse 5, which the card doesn't cite. The joke should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward, such as one that sets up the people speaking against God and Moses, or the card should be cut.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'Snakes in the camp, and people bitten and dying,' repeats what cards 8 and 9 just asked and answered. That makes it recap instead of forward movement. The card should start right at verse 7, with the people coming to Moses.

The joke is muddled. 'Mine would've been right there too' is unclear: right where? It can also read as if Moses was crying, which the text never says. A stranger would say 'huh?' The line needs one clear image built on the core action of praying for people who just spoke against you.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The two blanks, 'no ___ or ___', are fixed to bread in blank 1 and water in blank 2. A baker who places 'water' then 'bread' has the meaning right but would be marked wrong. Nothing in the reasoning separates the two orders.
findings.question: When two blanks hold interchangeable items in a list, should either order count as right, or should the card be reworded so only one order makes sense?
